  "situation": "The Study Team is considering how to organize the Defense Intelligence Agency mission. The choices include retaining the mission in one agency, returning it to the Military Departments, or consolidating additional department-wide activities in the Defense Intelligence Agency. The existing arrangement requires additional resources and authority to carry out the intelligence function. The alternatives raise concerns about efficiency, coordination, analytical duplication, and the management of shared intelligence production. The Study Team must also weigh the feasibility and effects of broader consolidation.",
  "question": "What should the Study Team do about the organization of the Defense Intelligence Agency mission?",

      "kind": "situation",
      "status": "assessed",

      "fact": "Returning the mission to the Military Departments is assessed to fragment resources, promote analytical duplication, and provide decision makers with uncoordinated intelligence data.",

      "fact": "One alternative would place in the Defense Intelligence Agency department-wide intelligence production, processing, and infrastructure activities that do not directly support the U.S. Commands or their Component Commands and are common to more than one Military Department.",

      "kind": "situation",
      "status": "confirmed",
      "fact": "The largest Military Department production activities are Scientific and Technical Intelligence Centers, which support national and Military Department-specific requirements under the Defense Intelligence Agency's functional management and the Director of DIA's resource management as General Defense Intelligence Program Manager.",

      "kind": "situation",
